caption: The drawing depicts a wooden double-door with four rectangular panels on each door. The panels are bordered with a light blue-gray trim, while the inner sections of each panel are a reddish-brown wood with visible grain and wear. Each door shows signs of aging and use, including cracks and discoloration. There is a small metal bell attached to the upper left door by a string, and a rope or pull cord hangs below it. The bottom left panel of the left door contains a circular hole. The door is set within a light-colored, off-white stucco wall that has subtle cracks and patches of faint pink lines around the doorway, suggesting masonry joints or structural features. Below the door is a small patio made of reddish-brown bricks, with the bricks drawn in detail in the immediate foreground and fading in color at the edges. The overall composition focuses on the central placement of the door within a textured, mostly plain background.
title: Church Door (Interior)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
